title: Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd - 543300 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 record revenue of ₹1,272 cr (+47% YoY) and EBITDA margin 24.4%, but commodity and mix pressure persists; management says EBITDA band is 23–25% post railway deal, with ~₹1,270 cr cash and order book ₹237 bn.

summary.headline: Sona Comstar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% YoY to ₹1,272 crore, a record quarter, though EBITDA margin fell 2.7pp to 24.4%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 posted record revenue (₹1,272 crore, +47% YoY), record EBITDA (₹311 crore, +32%) and record PAT (₹192 crore, +17%), with BEV revenue of ₹359 crore at a record 39% share. Margins compressed on commodity inflation with pass-through lag, product mix (lower-margin traction motors and railways) and a PLI income base effect. Management won four new driveline orders, including three from European OEMs in one quarter, and said Europe's EV order flow is returning. Full-year FY26 revenue grew 26% to ₹4,475 crore, with EBITDA margin at 24.7% and adjusted PAT up 11%.

segments.name: Automotive BEV
segments.commentary: Q4 BEV revenue ₹359 crore (39% share, record); FY26 BEV revenue ₹1,154 crore (-6%), weak Q1 drove the full-year decline. 67 EV programs across 35 customers, 37 in production and 30 pending.

segments.name: Traction and suspension motors
segments.commentary: Traction motors about 10% of revenue. Suspension motors expected to grow 3-4x in FY27 volumes, reaching single digit share of revenue in FY26 and possibly double digits in FY27.

segments.name: Differential gears and assemblies
segments.commentary: Legacy products kept growing alongside new products. Q4 saw 7 non-EV differential gear programs from existing customers worth about ₹3 billion.

segments.name: Railway (acquired)
segments.commentary: Lower-margin, high-return business, consolidated during FY26 and funded with about ₹1,800 crore. Q4 approvals for electric control panels (first batch supplied) and HVAC (supply to start this quarter).

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Eastern markets were 60% of Q4 revenue vs 40% a year earlier. India exceeded 50% of mix for full year FY26.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin band guided at 23-25% post railway acquisition, replacing the earlier 24-26% band for the core business.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, freight, packaging, energy) expected to keep pressuring margins in the foreseeable future, as pass-through lags.
Haryana minimum wage hike effective 1 April 2026 expected to add labour cost; to be offset via productivity, tighter headcount addition and workload management.
Novelic India SOP for one customer expected at end of calendar 2026; Europe in-cabin safety NCAP requirement moved to 2027.

Railway growth over 3-5 years framed through capacity/process improvement, white-space variants and new products (HVAC needs about 3 years for full rolling stock coverage; electric panels 12-15 months).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex ₹369 crore; additional land bought for about ₹110 crore.
Gas requirement cut by nearly 20% at company level via electric heating, gas-flow optimisation and process changes; no production loss so far.
Traction motor capacity of about 1 million electric motors, reusable across customers with tweaks.
Fixed asset turnover fell to 2.9 due to new capitalisation and land purchase; expected to improve as FY26 capex generates revenue in FY27.
ROCE dipped due to fresh equity raised in September 2024; expected to improve over medium term as railway capital is deployed.
demand_pricing: Q4 wins: 4 driveline orders, including 3 from European OEMs (highest ever in a quarter from Europe, first EV win from Europe in about 4 years) and 1 hybrid platform.
FY26: 31 new programs won and 3 new customers added; order book roughly flat YoY after a Q2 correction tied to one model.
Pricing: company says a large part of commodity inflation is passed through with a lag; the remainder hits margins.
Demand: management cites March 2026 BEV sales up about 45% in EU and India e-car and e-2W up 65% and 45%; April trending above 50% in India.
US: Section 232 tariffs (25%) unchanged; management says revenue and margins from US not materially affected.
China: one large Chinese EV customer supplied; management sees entry into China-for-China supply chain as hard for now.

qa_highlights.question: Opportunity from European peer bankruptcies and asset sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says some opportunities already flowing (recent wins); Europe still a good place to win business over the next 12 months, with no material change to the opportunity set.

qa_highlights.question: Novelic India progress and ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Entity set up in India, launch process started for one customer, SOP at end of calendar 2026 using in-house SMT line. Management declined to give kit value or pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity impact of about 80bps in Q4 – normalising?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: about half mix and half commodity; largely lag in material pass-through. Commodity prices still rising, so margin pressure persists until inflation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Suspension motor growth and railway growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Suspension motors to grow 3-4x in volume; traction motors to grow at high double digits. Railway growth over 3-5 years via capacity improvement, white-space variants and new products. No formal growth guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Market size of new railway products?
qa_highlights.answer: HVAC market about ₹2,000-2,500 crore; electric panels about ₹1,500 crore. Full coverage of rolling stock takes 12-15 months for panels and at least 3 years for HVAC.

qa_highlights.question: Margin band and M&A pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin band now 23-25% post railway acquisition. Over 100 M&A opportunities evaluated in 3 years, one acted on; no reportable deal in pipeline.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, energy, freight) and lagged pass-through could keep EBITDA margin under pressure.
Haryana wage hike from 1 April 2026 adds labour cost; watch headcount discipline.
Gas availability constraint; ~20% gas cut so far with no loss to date.
Concentration in EVs (70% of order book) and shifting EV subsidies; management says most orders are in low-subsidy regions.
Railway integration: lower margins and returns still building; ROCE and fixed asset turnover pressure until capital is deployed.
US tariff regime and demand effects of inflation; Section 232 tariffs unchanged at 25%.
Rare earth magnet policy: company says it uses no heavy rare earth magnets currently.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, wins and balance sheet, but openly cautious on commodity-driven margin pressure and evasive on commodity timing and tariff specifics ("multi-trillion dollar question"). Management frequently cites deliberate, long-cycle product development.
key_quotes: Q4 was the best ever quarter across the board.
Frankly, this is the first EV order win from Europe in almost 4 years.
It will improve returns because from a return perspective, they're very, very high return, businesses.

Operating cash ₹659 crore; capex ₹369 crore; FCF ₹290 crore

Railway HVAC supply starting this quarter (existing acquired business, not new capacity)

growth.why: No explicit FY27 revenue growth guidance given; EBITDA margin band held at 23-25% post railway acquisition, with Q4 revenue +47% YoY (railway consolidation included) and a net order book of ₹237 billion (70% EV) roughly flat YoY, 31 new programs won in FY26, and 4 driveline wins in Q4, with suspension motors guided to grow 3-4x in FY27 volumes.
